failure_modes: Selective depletion of biologically important EV subpopulations (loss of potency despite apparent analytic improvement).

Membrane perturbation/damage during depletion that either (a) exposes cargo making captured signal detergent/protease-sensitive in a non-informative way, or (b) fragments EVs into particles still counted by NTA/TRPS but lacking intact membranes (false particle-count recovery).
Residual depletion-reagent interference with immuno-capture or protection assays producing false-positive co-localization or detergent-sensitivity results that pass qualitative gates.
Insufficient particle/mass yield after depletion that renders the bounded fraction non-manufacturable despite meeting analytic identity (false operational success).
Spike-in controls that do not match endogenous EV biophysical/biochemical properties fail to reveal assay failures or selective losses (undetected assay blind spots).

Qualitative (non-numeric) pass/fail gating masks gradual but meaningful differences between arms (e.g., partial loss of specific subtypes or dose-dependent yield losses), making effects unmeasurable or irreproducible across lots.

Improved in vitro orthogonal identity that nevertheless does not predict in vivo recoverability or delivery after intranasal administration — species, formulation, or device barriers (as seen in NHP data) prevent translation of the analytically bounded fraction to detectable brain exposure.

Cross-species generalizability failure: materials that look good by the orthogonal assays in rodent-scale testing may still fail to be detectable or active in larger animals or humans due to clearance or retention in nasal passages.

Inadequate assay specificity: capture reagents (e.g., anti-CD63/9/81) may bind soluble fragments or complexes remaining after depletion, generating misleading capture signal that is not membrane-protected.
Qualitative endpoints preclude establishing quantitative release/specification criteria later, hampering comparability and regulatory acceptance.
strongest_objection: The single strongest bounded failure mode is assay-confounding removal or alteration of true EV content by the pre-SEC affinity depletion step such that downstream orthogonal readouts (capture co-localization and detergent/protease sensitivity) appear improved but do not reflect preservation of the native, bioactive EV population. This can occur either because (A) the depletion resin selectively strips EV-surface proteins or EV-associated cargo/coat layers (removing subpopulations that carry key markers or activity), (B) the depletion process perturbs membrane integrity (creating detergent-/protease-sensitive artifacts or destroying membrane protection), or (C) residual depletion reagents or altered buffer conditions create assay interference that mimics capture-positive, membrane-protected signal despite loss or modification of authentic EVs. Any of these produces a misleading “pass” that is analytically bounded but biologically irrelevant and/or non-manufacturable, and would not be detected reliably by the proposed qualitative pass/fail gating even with spike-ins.
